item.title: Current Events - August 26, 2026
item.description:
August 26, 2026 (2026-08-26) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • 2026 Iran–Oman negotiations
          • The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps say Iran and Oman have agreed to share revenues from the Strait of Hormuz and define their respective maritime areas, while negotiations continue over reopening the waterway amid the war. (AFP via The Borneo Post)
          • Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says that Iran will not allow military vessels to transit through the strait under the proposed agreement. (AP) (Military.com)
    • Gaza war
      • The Israel Defense Forces says that they have killed several Hamas members in airstrikes in the Gaza Strip city of Jabalia, including on a structure allegedly used as a storage facility for weapons. (The Jerusalem Post)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • An overnight Ukrainian drone attack "completely destroys" a Wildberries depot in Tambov Oblast, Russia. (Reuters)
      • A man and a 14-year-old child are killed in Lipetsk Oblast, and a woman is killed in Belgorod Oblast, in Ukrainian drone strikes. The Russian defence ministry says its forces have shot down 426 Ukrainian drones overnight. (Al Jazeera)
    • Luhansk Oblast campaign
      • Nine people are killed after a Ukrainian strike on a bus in Russian-occupied Luhansk. (Reuters)

Arts and culture

  • 2026 anti-immigrant movement and xenophobia in South Africa
    • A spokesperson for Malian singer Salif Keita confirms that he has cancelled all upcoming concerts in South Africa over its response to anti-migrant protests in the country. (Channels TV) (Arbiterz)

Business and economy

  • American multinational company General Mills announces that they have removed artificial colors from their cereals including Lucky Charms and Trix. (NBC News)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Nepal floods
    • Flash floods and mudslides along the Trishuli River impact Nepal and Tibet. At least 160 people are killed, hundreds are injured and 463 others, including over 200 tourists, are reported missing in Nepal, while Chinese Communist Party officials report three deaths and 265 missing in Tibet, severely affecting Gyirong County and its port. (AFP via Jamaica Observer) (AP) (BBC News)
    • Nepali officials say bridges, roads, power stations, and entire villages have been swept away by the flash flooding with some areas still completely cut-off from search and rescue efforts. (Al Jazeera) (The National)
  • At least 15 infants are killed and another is injured after a fire at a state-run hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan. (The Globe and Mail) (The Guardian)
  • Twelve people are killed and at least 54 others are injured as wildfires spread across northeastern Algeria during a severe heat wave, with deaths reported in Béjaïa, Jijel, and Tizi Ouzou provinces. (AFP via Gulf News)

Health and environment

  • Nineteen cases of Japanese encephalitis are confirmed in Madhesh Province, Nepal, causing six deaths. (Nepal News)
  • The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves the daraxonrasib drug as a treatment for metastatic pancreatic cancer, making it the first RAS inhibitor drug to be approved for the disease. This came after a previous study showed that it nearly doubled the survival rate for patients compared to chemotherapy. (The Guardian) (Reuters)

International relations

  • South Korea–United States relations, Japan–United States relations
    • The U.S. Pacific Command announces that the United States will conduct trilateral military exercises with South Korea's armed forces and Japan's self-defense forces despite U.S. president Donald Trump scaling back on the recent Ulchi-Freedom Guardian exercises. (AA via TRT World) (Korea Herald)

Law and crime

  • Aftermath of the September 11 attacks
    • The U.S. military trial for al-Qaeda militant Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the alleged mastermind of the September 11 attacks, is set for June 2028 alongside three co-conspirators. (NBC News) (Sky News)
  • Lawsuits involving Meta Platforms
    • Meta Platforms agrees to pay up to $16.7 billion to settle claims by 29 U.S. states over alleged harms to young users and to impose new usage limits and safeguards for teenagers on its social media platforms Facebook and Instagram. (AFP via ABS-CBN News)
  • Terrorism in the United States
    • The United States designates the Italy-based Autistici/Inventati, the UK-based Palestine Action, and pro-Palestinian group Masar Badil as terrorist organizations, citing alleged involvement in politically motivated violence and extremist activity. (AFP via France 24)
  • Russia orders the arrest of German Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung journalist Michael Martens [de], charging him in absentia over comments interpreted as calling for the killing of Russians, a crime punishable by up to six years in prison. (News.az)
  • Two people are killed and nine others are seriously injured in a vehicle-ramming attack against pedestrians after a fight near a train station in Caen, Normandy, France. The perpetrator is arrested. (France 24)

Politics and elections

  • Immigration policy of the second Trump administration
    • The United States Department of State suspends immigrant visa appointments at all embassies and consulates worldwide while training consular staff on screening applicants for potential dependence on public benefits. (AFP via ABS-CBN News)
  • Deogratius Ndejembi is appointed as Vice President of Tanzania, replacing Emmanuel Nchimbi who resigned yesterday. (The Tanzania Times)

Sports

  • Pro Bowl Games
    • In American football, the National Football League announces the elimination of the Pro Bowl Games. (The New York Times) (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - September 02, 2026
item.description:
September 2, 2026 (2026-09-02) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Israeli–Palestinian conflict
    • Israeli settler violence
      • Palestinian officials say two teenagers were killed during an incident involving Israeli settlers and soldiers in al-Mughayyir, Ramallah and al-Bireh Governorate, West Bank. The villiage council states that the Palestinian teenagers were killed when they were trying to prevent the Israeli settlers from stealing livestock. Israel's military says troops shot stone-throwers while protecting an Israeli civilian and police retrieving livestock. (BBC News)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • The World Food Programme reports that an airstrike hit two UN food aid trucks in Dilling, South Kordofan, Sudan, over the weekend, destroying emergency supplies. (AFP via Arab News) (Sudan Tribune)
  • Insurgency in Balochistan
    • Twenty-one insurgents and six Pakistani personnel, including five security forces and a customs official, are killed in separate shootouts across multiple districts in Balochistan, Pakistan. (Dawn)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • The global stock index rises following recent declines amidst the war in Iran including renewed tensions with the Japanese yen gaining against the United States dollar. (Reuters)
  • The Dutch central bank reallocates 86 tonnes of gold reserves from Ottawa, Canada, and New York City, United States, to London, United Kingdom, increasing the share held there to 32.1%, citing "increasing geopolitical unrest". (AFP via France 24) (Seoul Economic Daily)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Dahab-Nuweiba bus crash
    • At least 22 people, including ten Jordanians, are killed and 28 others are injured in a bus accident in South Sinai, Egypt. (AFP via France 24)
  • The MV Tuğberk İmamoğlu cargo ship sinks in the Marmara Sea after a collision with an oil tanker, leaving ten people missing. (Euronews)
  • At least 13 people are killed and five others sustain critical injuries after two minivans collide head-on in Greater Accra, Ghana. (Xinhua)
  • Five people are killed and 20 others injured after a passenger bus collides with a tanker truck on the National Highway 39 in Rewa District, Madhya Pradesh, India. (Times of India)
  • An explosion at the Augsburg train station in Swabia, Germany, injures two people. The cause is unknown. (Euronews)
  • A crew member is killed, six others are missing, and one is rescued when a tugboat capsizes and sinks off the coast of Busan, South Korea. (AP)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents
    • Following the drone attacks at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month, German security authorities are focusing on several suspects with ties to Russia. According to investigations by the NDR, WDR, and SZ, the suspects are two men from Belarus and Lithuania who are also said to hold Russian passports. (AFP via France 24) (DW)
  • Birthright citizenship in the United States
    • U.S. federal judge Deborah Boardman of Maryland's district court blocks an attempt by the Trump administration from implementing an executive order aimed at ending birthright citizenship in the country. (The New York Times) (Reuters)
  • A Maltese jury acquits businessman Yorgen Fenech of complicity in the 2017 car-bomb killing of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia and of criminal association, finding him not guilty by an 8–1 vote. (AP via NPR)
  • Three people are killed, including the perpetrator, and six others are injured in a mass shooting in Loring Park, Minneapolis, United States. (AP) (DW)
  • Digital rights organization SHARE Foundation documents at least 14 Serbian students and opposition activists targeted with Pegasus or NoviSpy spyware in 2026, while Citizen Lab confirms Pegasus infection in at least one case. (Financial Times)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Estonian presidential election
    • Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, the only candidate, is elected by the Riigikogu as President of Estonia. She will be sworn into office on October 12, succeeding Alar Karis. (ERR) (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2027 U.S. Open Cup
    • In association football, Major League Soccer announces that all 27 teams from the United States will return to the U.S. Open Cup beginning in 2027, making it the first full participation in the tournament since 2023. (ESPN) (The Guardian)

item.title: Current Events - August 25, 2026
item.description:
August 25, 2026 (2026-08-25) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • 2026 Iran–Oman negotiations
          • Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and Omani foreign minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi say that Iran and Oman have discussed a proposal to establish a temporary joint shipping route for ships in the Strait of Hormuz. (CNBC)
        • 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
          • United States president Donald Trump and the United States Navy say that all mines have been cleared from the Strait of Hormuz. (Al-Monitor)
        • The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reports that an oil tanker has been struck by a unknown projectile off the coast of Oman near the strait. No casualties are reported. (AFP via Arab News) (Gulf News)
      • Analysis of the 2026 Iran war
        • The Wall Street Journal reports that U.S. president Trump launched Operation Epic Fury in February despite warnings from U.S. vice president JD Vance and then-intelligence director Tulsi Gabbard. (Middle East Monitor)
    • Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
      • The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announce they have officially dissolved and completed a merger with the Syrian army following the end of the civil war in 2024. (AP)
    • Gaza war
      • The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet say that they have struck five Hamas weapons storage systems and a launch site in Gaza, including in mosques. (Ynetnews)
  • Operation Southern Spear
    • United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
      • The U.S. military launches a strike against a vessel in the Caribbean Sea allegedly carrying drug smugglers, killing four people. (The Guardian)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign
      • Around 27 people, including four children, are reported to be killed by Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North (SPLM-N) militants in the South Kordofan areas of Kadugli and Abu Hitan. (Middle East Monitor)
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • Sudan’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Welfare reports that 224 cases of child sexual violence have been documented since the conflict. (Sudan Tribune)

Arts and culture

  • AI boom, Artificial intelligence in music
    • The Australian Recording Industry Association bans wholly AI-generated music from appearing on its charts starting in September 2026. The ruling aims to distinguish fully AI-generated music and AI-assisted music, where the track is human-created but uses AI as a supporting tool. (DW)

Business and economy

  • Canada–United States relations
    • 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
      • Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on about US$20 billion worth of U.S. annual imports in response to the 50% tariffs by U.S. president Donald Trump and his administration. (Reuters)
  • Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Boycott of Russia and Belarus, Belarus–Latvia relations, Latvia–Russia relations
      • Latvia's cabinet ministry announces that the country will ban imported goods from Belarus and Russia starting September 1. (LIGA)
  • South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor Company reaches a deal to end a month of walkouts by workers. (AFP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Flores earthquake
    • The toll from the earthquake in Flores, Indonesia, ten days ago, increases to 103 people dead and 1,666 injured. (Detik News)
  • 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
    • The death toll for the earthquakes in Venezuela this June exceeds past 6,500, with a total of 6,509 deaths reported. (The Straits Times)
  • At least 40 people are injured and over 300 homes are damaged in a tornado in Pomas, Occitania, France. (DW)
  • El Salvador declares a nationwide red alert for meteorological and agricultural drought, while Panama declares an El Niño emergency as severe dry conditions damage crops and reduce traffic through the Panama Canal. (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)

International relations

  • Russia–United States relations
    • U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) director John Ratcliffe visits Moscow, Russia, on an unscheduled military flight to meet with Russian intelligence officials, marking the first known visit by a U.S. CIA director to Russia since 2021. (Al Jazeera) (BBC News)
    • The Wall Street Journal reports Ratcliffe's visit was to formally warn Russia against attacking NATO after military intelligence suggested Russia is preparing for a "limited assault" on a NATO member state. (AFP via CNA) (The Wall Street Journal)
  • Israel and the United Nations, Israeli occupation of the West Bank
    • The Israel Defense Forces take control of the UNRWA's vocational training centre in Qalandia, East Jerusalem, West Bank, and begin removing the United Nations agency under legislation banning its operations in Israel. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary
    • Hungary foreign and deputy prime minister Anita Orbán files a criminal complaint against the government of former prime minister Viktor Orbán (no relation) over its purchase of 300 billion Ft (US$965 million) in ventilators during the COVID-19 pandemic in the country. (AP) (Reuters)
  • Lawsuits involving TikTok
    • Brazil's national data protection authority fines TikTok R$153.7 million (US$29.9 million) for inadequate child-safety measures and orders its developer, ByteDance, to delete improperly collected data and strengthen protections for users under 16. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • Hijab and burqa controversies in Europe
    • The Grand Council of Aargau votes 78–54 to ban Islamic hijabs for girls aged under 16 in the Swiss canton of Aargau. The motion was sponsored by the Radical-Liberal Party. (Swiss Info)
  • Emmanuel Nchimbi announces his resignation as the vice president of Tanzania. (Africanews) (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 WNBA season
    • In basketball, the Women's National Basketball Association's Chicago Sky bans Enes Kanter Freedom from attending home games following his altercation with Natasha Cloud. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - September 01, 2026
item.description:
September 1, 2026 (2026-09-01) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • September 2026 United States strikes on Iran
          • The United States carries out additional airstrikes against Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corp (IRGC) targets in Iran, in response to recent attempted attacks on commercial shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and on U.S. troops in the region, according to the U.S. Central Command. Five members of the IRGC Aerospace Force are killed in Kermanshah. (Al Jazeera) (BBC News) (CNN)
      • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
        • Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says that his country is ready to return to the Islamabad Memorandum signed in June if the United States does the same amidst renewed fighting between the two countries. (Fortune)
      • 2026 Sirik wedding airstrike
        • Iranian state media reports that five civilians were killed and 63 more were wounded at a wedding party at a home in Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, during an American airstrike against Iranian military targets. (Al Jazeera)
    • Gaza war
      • Four people are killed in Israeli strikes during a ground operation in Gaza. Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu says that Israeli forces captured a senior Hamas internal security official in the operation. (AFP via France 24)
    • War against the Islamic State, Yemeni Civil War
      • Abu Hudhayfah al-Ansari, the spokesperson for the Islamic State, is killed during a security operation by the Yemeni Armed Forces. (Voice of Emirates)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Kyiv strikes
      • Ukrainian officials say that Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas killed at least 12 people, including an Indian national, and injure dozens, while damaging residential buildings and other civilian infrastructure. (NDTV)

Arts and culture

  • The 75,000-seater Kingdome, built by the Christian sect Kingdom of Jesus Christ, opens in Davao City, Philippines, becoming the largest indoor arena in the world. It surpasses the 55,000-seater Philippine Arena in Bulacan. (Manila Bulletin) (MindaNews)

Business and economy

  • Senegal hidden debt scandal
    • The International Monetary Fund reaches a staff-level agreement with Senegal on a new US$2.2 billion, 36-month loan program supporting economic reforms after an earlier arrangement was suspended over previously unreported government debt. (AFP via France 24)
  • Ghana begins requiring artisanal doré bars purchased by privately financed gold buyers to undergo domestic refining before export, with GoldBod considering export applications only after processing at approved refineries. (Reuters)
  • Japan eases overtime enforcement by ending pressure on companies with special labor-management agreements to keep monthly overtime below 45 hours, as businesses face labor shortages. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Nepal floods
    • Nepal–South Korea relations
      • South Korea's foreign ​ministry announces that the country will deploy a 44-member emergency relief team to Nepal to support search-and-rescue operations after flash floods hit the South Asian country. (The Korea Herald) (Reuters)
    • The Nepali Army reports that around 119 people have been rescued. (The Guardian)
  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Tropical Storm Edouard makes landfall on the Gulf Coast of the United States. (CNN)
  • Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured when a speeding passenger van, with an Ipil–Pagadian route, crashes into a motorcycle and a wing van in Dumalinao, Zamboanga del Sur, Philippines. (Philippine Daily Inquirer)
  • Four people are killed and more than ten others are injured when a car crashes into a gathering of government and military supporters in Mashhad, Razavi Khorasan, Iran. Traffic police arrest the driver and say the incident was unintentional. (Reuters)
  • Six pilgrims are killed and 14 others sustain serious injuries after a pickup truck carrying devotees collides with a truck along an expressway in Palwal district, Haryana, India. (The Times of India)

Health and environment

  • The New Zealand Conservation Department reports that the amount of endangered Kākāpō species have reached 325 in the country following the addition of 90 chicks, exceeding 300 for the first time in 75 years. (The Guardian) (NBC News)

International relations

  • Germany–Russia relations, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
    • 2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents
      • Germany raises its threat assessment to "high", orders the closure of Russia's consulate in Bonn, North Rhine-Westphalia, and the Russian House in Berlin, and tightens entry controls for Russian nationals after attributing the drone attacks at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Saxony, last month to Russia. (CNN)
  • Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
    • Peru's foreign ministry says that the country has cut off ties with Iran, accusing it of escalating the war in the Middle East. (AP in Spanish) (Al-Arabiya)

Law and crime

  • Assassination of Charlie Kirk
    • An American judge rules that the case against Tyler James Robinson, accused of murdering political activist Charlie Kirk in September 2025, can go to trial, citing sufficient probable cause. (BBC News) (CNN)
  • LGBTQ rights in the United States
    • The U.S. Department of Justice files a lawsuit against the public schools district of Kansas City, Kansas, over its policies that allow transgender students to share their preferred name, gender, and pronouns with school staff. (KCUR) (Reuters)
  • A Honduran judge dismisses a corruption case against former president Juan Orlando Hernández, ruling that he neither authorized nor managed the public funds allegedly diverted to finance his 2013 presidential campaign. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • Death and state funeral of Harald V
    • Haakon VIII takes the oath as King of Norway before the Storting following the death of his father, Harald V. His daughter, Ingrid Alexandra, takes the oath as Crown Princess. (AP) (Reuters)
  • Nicaragua's National Assembly approves on first reading a constitutional amendment barring opposition parties from elections and extending presidential and other elected terms from six to seven years. A second legislative vote is required for ratification. (Reuters)
  • Former British prime minister Keir Starmer resigns as a member of the House of Commons for his appointment to the Chiltern Hundreds; a by-election will be held to fill his parlimentary seat of Holborn and St Pancras. (Al Jazeera) (BBC News)

Science and technology

  • Syria and weapons of mass destruction
    • The International Atomic Energy Agency reports that Syria's former government under Bashar al-Assad failed to declare nuclear material and facilities, confirming that infrastructure at Deir ez-Zor is consistent with an unfinished nuclear reactor and identifying about 73 tonnes of natural uranium. (AFP via France 24)
  • The Turkish foreign ministry reports that Turkey has joined the U.S.-led Artemis Accords, becoming the 71st country to do so. (AA) (Firstpost)

Sports

  • In baseball, the Los Angeles Angels of the MLB are sold to Stan Kroenke of Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for an unspecified price, ending 23 years of ownership by Arte Moreno. The deal faces pending regulatory review and is expected to be complete by 2027. (CNBC) (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - August 27, 2026
item.description:
August 27, 2026 (2026-08-27) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Gaza–Israel conflict
      • Gaza war
        • Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
          • Three Palestinians are reported to be killed in strikes in the Gaza Strip, violating the October 2025 ceasefire. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
        • Gaza war hostage crisis
          • The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) and its Spokesperson's Unit confirms Al-Qassam Brigades commander Ismail Mohammad Ibrahim Barim, who held Edan Alexander, Avera Mengistu, and Matan Zangauker as hostages, was killed in a strike in Khan Yunis. (The Times of Israel) (Israel National News) (The Jerusalem Post)
        • The IDF also confirms that they have recently killed two Hamas militants that invaded the Re'im Base in Re'im during the October 7 attacks in separate strikes in the Gaza Strip, including a body guard to former leader Yahya Sinwar and a Nukhba forces militant. (The Times of Israel)
      • It is reported that Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu held secret meetings with Hamas during the 2014 Gaza War. The Prime Minister's Office denies the reports. (The Times of Israel) (Ynetnews)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
        • Qatar as a mediator in conflict
          • Qatari prime minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani talks with Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi in Tehran, including on the Strait of Hormuz and efforts to end the war. (Al Jazeera)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
          • United States Central Command commander Brad Cooper says that the military has cleared all Iranian naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and its routes. (The Hill)
        • Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei says that Iran is preparing a set of conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz after mediators called for them to do so. (Reuters)
        • The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reports that a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by an "unknown projectile", causing a fire that was later extinguished. (Marine Insight)
  • Sudanese Civil Wars
    • Sudanese civil war
      • Blue Nile campaign
        • Sudan's army repels a Rapid Support Forces attack on the town of Al-Keli in the Blue Nile region. (Sudan Tribune)
      • Battle of Khartoum
        • Sudan's Security Affairs Coordination Committee lifts the curfew and state of emergency on the capital Khartoum after two years. (Middle East Monitor) (BBC)
      • Around 12 people are reported killed in a airstrike near border with Chad. (Al Jazeera)
    • Sudanese nomadic conflicts
      • Around 49 people are killed in a cattle raid on the Machar-Pakuek cattle camp in Mading Juer Boma in Tonj North County of South Sudan's Warrap state. (MENA via The New Arab)
  • Kivu conflict
    • M23 campaign
      • Four people are killed after an unconfirmed civilian or military airplane is shot down with a surface-to-air missile near Minembwe, Democratic Republic of the Congo. (Noveau Media)
  • Mexican drug war
    • NORAD and the U.S. Northern Command say that the U.S. military used a laser weapon against three drones belonging to Mexican drug cartels. (Military Times)

Business and economy

  • South Korean company SK Gas pays a record US$5.3 million for priority passage of the LPG tanker G. Spirit through the Panama Canal before El Niño-related transit restrictions reduced daily crossings. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • Wildfires in 2026
    • 2026 Canadian wildfires
      • In Canada, British Columbia ends its state of emergency previously imposed on August 8 in response to wildfires that killed one person. (The Canadian Press News) (CTV News)
      • A section of the Trans-Canada Highway in the Fraser Canyon reopens after being closed for seven weeks due to the wildfires. (Redfm) (CTV News)
    • Algerian president Abdelmadjid Tebboune declares three days of national mourning after 12 people were reported to be killed in wildfires in northeastern Jijel. (Africanews)
  • 2026 Flores earthquake
    • The death toll from the earthquake that struck the Flores island in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, rises to 111, with 176,000 people displaced. (A News) (AA)
  • 2026 Nepal floods
    • The United States Geological Survey says a glacial collapse and debris flow, not an earthquake, caused the seismic event near the Nepal–Tibet border and subsequent flooding that killed at least 392 people and left over 900 more missing. (BBC News)
  • Incidents at Six Flags parks
    • The X2 roller coaster at the Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park in Valencia, California, U.S., closes after a CNN investigation reported that two riders were recently hospitalized for brain injuries. (CNN) (The Guardian)
  • Six people die after a pump boat carrying 13 passengers capsizes while crossing the Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino, Zambales, Philippines. Three others remain missing. (The Philippine Star)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Democratic Republic of the Congo begins vaccination for the Ebola outbreak in Kisangani, Tshopo, with healthcare and front line workers among the first to receive the vaccine. (Africanews)
  • 2026 European heatwaves
    • Germany's Robert Koch Institute estimates 15,800 heat-related deaths during summer 2026, the highest total in a decade of monitoring, as repeated heat waves push temperatures above 40 °C (104 °F). (Kurdistan 24)

International relations

  • Malaysia–Myanmar relations
    • Malaysia says that 1,476 Burmese people will be voluntarily repatriated on September 29 in the first phase of a return program agreed with Myanmar, using Myanmar naval vessels. (AFP via The Manila Times)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Gosen-Neu Zittau school stabbing
    • Two people are killed in a stabbing at a private school in Gosen-Neu Zittau, Brandenburg, Germany. A suspect is arrested. (Xinhua)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Zambian general election
    • Zambian presidential candidate Brian Mundubile surrenders to police and is questioned over an alleged national security threat after two weeks in hiding following the disputed presidential election, in which he finished second. (AFP via France 24)
  • Forced contraception of women in Greenland
    • Denmark's parliament passes legislation granting 300,000 kr. (US$46,758) in compensation to each Greenlandic woman affected by non-consensual contraception administered under a Danish birth-control program in the 1960s and 1970s. (BBC News)
  • U.S. president Donald Trump signs an executive order directing federal agencies to call Lake Ontario "Lake America." The change applies only to U.S. federal usage; Canada need not adopt it, and no international authority exclusively determines names of shared waters. (AP) (The Guardian)
  • King Rukidi IV of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom, the youngest person to reign as a monarch, dies at the age of 34. (BBC News) (NTV Uganda)

Science and technology

  • August 2026 lunar eclipse
    • A near-total partial lunar eclipse occurs over Africa, the Americas, and Europe. (TimeandDate)
  • The Korea AeroSpace Administration says that the Nuri will launch 15 satellites, a record, into space from the Naro Space Center in South Korea's Goheung County on October 7. (Korea Times) (Yonhap)

Sports

  • 2026 Diamond League
    • In athletics, Brazilian Alison dos Santos and American Masai Russell break the world records in men's 400 metres hurdles (45.80 seconds) and women's 100 metres hurdles (12.09 seconds), respectively, at the 2026 Weltklasse Zürich in Zurich, Switzerland. (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - September 03, 2026
item.description:
September 3, 2026 (2026-09-03) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war, United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war
        • Iran's military launches drones and missiles on Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates, targeting United States military facilities and equipment to retaliate for the recent U.S. bombardment of Iran that killed at least 19 people. (AFP via South China Morning Post)
      • 2026 Sirik wedding airstrike
        • U.S. vice president JD Vance says that the country will investigate its military strike against a wedding in Bandar Sirik that killed five people. (Middle East Eye) (The Jerusalem Post)
    • 2026 Lebanon war
      • 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire
        • Israel releases prisoner Malek Ghazi and hands him over to the Lebanese army, the first release since the war started in March, as part of an effort to revive peace talks. (AP) (Arab News)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • The Houthis launch an offensive in western Yemen, clashing with the Yemeni Armed Forces and aiming to reach and cut the road linking Taiz to Al-Makha district. Fourteen balistic missiles and several drones are launched in Taiz and Hodeidah. At least 18 Houthi fighters and 13 government troops are killed in the clashes. (Al Jazeera)
  • Russo–Ukrainian war
    • Kharkiv Oblast campaign
      • Russian forces say they have captured several settlements in northeastern Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, encircling Ukrainian forces. (ISW)
    • The Security Service of Ukraine open fire against agents of the Main Directorate of Intelligence in Kyiv during a search at an apartment related to an arrest against a Russian national fighting for Ukraine, wounding three people. (The Guardian)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Sudanese refugee crisis
      • The International Organization for Migration reports the first operation of a voluntary repatriation flight for stranded migrants in Khartoum, Sudan, since the war started three years ago. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Colombian conflict
    • A Colombian judge orders president Abelardo de la Espriella's government to suspend airstrikes on guerrilla camps in the Guaviare Department when intelligence indicated that minors may be present, after recent bombings killed at least three teenagers. (AFP via France 24)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • Five people are killed and several other residents are abducted during a bandit attack in Kebbe, Sokoto State, Nigeria. (Daily Post Nigeria)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • 2026 East Malaysia haze, Endangerment of orangutans
      • Authorities in Indonesia rescue a mother orangutan and her baby from wildfire smoke on the island of Borneo. (The Borneo Post)
  • 2026 Nepal floods
    • United Arab Emirates president Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan announces that the country will deploy an emergency relief mission to Nepal to support people affected by the deadly floods and landslides. (Gulf News)
  • At least 37 people are killed after inhaling petroleum fumes while allegedly siphoning fuel from an illegally tapped pipeline in Rivers State, Nigeria. (AFP via France 24)
  • Six crew members are referred to court as part of the investigation into the ship collision in the Sea of Marmara yesterday, while the search continues for the ten Turkish crew members aboard the sunken MV Tuğberk İmamoğlu cargo ship. (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • 2026 East Malaysia haze
    • Malaysia's disaster agency, meteorological agency, and air force launch cloud-seeding operations in Sarawak to reduce haze and increase water reserves. (AFP via France 24)

International relations

  • Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
    • Syrian chemical weapons program, Use of chemical weapons in the Syrian civil war
      • Officials at a United Nations Security Council meeting say that Syria has started the process of destroying clandestine chemical weapons from former president Bashar al-Assad's regime. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • Germany–Russia relations
    • 2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents
      • Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov says that Russia will close Goethe-Institut cultural centers in Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Yekaterinburg in response to Germany closing Russia's consulate in Bonn and the Russian House in Berlin following the drone attacks at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month. (AP)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Tacloban school shooting, 2026 Ateneo de Zamboanga shooting
    • The Philippine education department initiates nationwide school safety drills to prepare students and staff for armed intruders, involving police and emergency responders after two school shooting incidents. (AFP via France 24)
  • A court in Moscow, Russia, places children's hospice founder Lida Moniava under judicial supervision, imposing a nightly curfew, internet ban, and contact restrictions over a 2023 post prosecutors said spread false information about the military. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2025–2026 United States redistricting
    • In the United States, the Supreme Court of Missouri blocks the use of a congressional map intended to favor Republicans, despite the map having already been used for primary elections in the state. A referendum on the 2025 map will appear on the ballot for the November election in the state. (AP) (The Guardian)

Science and technology

  • AI boom
    • OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra, the latest version of ChatGPT. (AFP via ABS-CBN News) (Axios)
  • The BepiColombo begins its final mission to Mercury, eight years after its launch by the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency. (Space.com)
  • NASA discovers a 10–sided pattern on the south pole of Saturn using its Hubble Space Telescope from the Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, United States. (The Peninsula) (ScienceDaily)

Sports

  • In association football, the French Football Federation upholds Bordeaux's relegation to Régional 1, the sixth tier of the French football league system, rejecting the club's request for reinstatement in National 2 following its exclusion from national competitions over financial concerns. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - August 30, 2026
item.description:
August 30, 2026 (2026-08-30) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
        • Iran launches ballistic missiles at U.S. military bases in Jordan. (Reuters)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • A spokesperson for the United States Central Command reports that the U.S. military has launched strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers at Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz that were used by Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, its first strikes against the country since July. (Axios) (NBC News)
    • Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
      • Syrian security forces says that they have killed Firas Abdul Karim Hammoud, a army commander who served under ousted former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad, after he opened fire on forces as they tried to arrest him. (Asharq Al Awsat)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Ukrainian missile strike on Belgorod, Russia, kills two people and injures 16 others, according to regional acting governor Alexander Shuvaev. (Reuters) (Xinhua)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign, Battle of Barah
      • Sudan's doctors network reports that five civilians are killed and thousands are displaced during attacks by Rapid Support Forces in Bara, North Kordofan. (Sudan Tribune)
  • 2026 Nigerien coup attempt
    • Niger's army says that they have regained control of an airbase after it was attacked by mutinous soldiers yesterday. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • 2026 East Malaysia haze, Endangerment of orangutans
      • An orangutan named Sampurna is reported to be rescued from a haze fire zone in Ketapang, West Kalimantan, on Indonesia's Borneo island. (Reuters)
    • The Japanese military ship JS Kunisaki departs from a port in Kure, Hiroshima, to help fight wildfires in Indonesia. (Tempo)
  • 2026 Grand Canyon flood
    • The body of one man is found near the Colorado River while 15 other people remain missing after a flash flood at Bright Angel Creek in the Grand Canyon in Arizona, United States. (Euronews)
  • Sinking of the Filo Jet
    • At least eight people are killed and 18 others are missing when a passenger ferry sailing from Northern Cyprus to Turkey capsizes in the eastern Mediterranean sea. The ship was carrying 259 passengers and 8 crew members, of which 237 people have been rescued. (Sky News) (Reuters)
  • The body of the last missing individual aboard a boat capsized on Thursday on Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino, Zambales, Philippines, is recovered, concluding search operations with the final death toll at nine. (Philippine Daily Inquirer)

International relations

  • 2026 state visit by Xi Jinping to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt
    • Chinese leader Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan arrive in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, for the upcoming Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit and a state visit. (AFP via RFI) (Xinhua)

Law and crime

  • One person is killed and five others are injured in a mass shooting at a rave in Aarau, Aargau, Switzerland. The perpetrator is on the run. (CNN)
  • Two people are killed and nine injured during a mass shooting at a gathering in Trenton, New Jersey, United States. (AA) (NBC News)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Guinea-Bissau constitutional referendum
    • Bissau-Guineans vote on a constitutional referendum that proposes to expand presidential powers. (AP)
  • The Korean Central News Agency reports that general No Kwang-chol has been dismissed as defence minister of North Korea, with Korean People's Army General Political Bureau director Kim Song-gi replacing him. (AFP via CNA) (NK News)
  • The Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile is charged with treason, amid heightened political tensions.(BBC News)

Science and technology

  • NASA launches the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a Falcon Heavy rocket from Florida, United States, to survey the universe, study dark matter and dark energy, and search for exoplanets and supernovae. (AFP via France 24) (Space.com)

Sports

  • 2026 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup
    • In field hockey, Germany defeats Spain 1–0 in the final to secure their fourth FIH Men's World Cup title. (Reuters)
  • 2026 World Rowing Championships
    • In rowing, the 2026 World Championships conclude in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with the host nation as the most successful team with 4 gold medals and 10 medals overall. (BBC Sport) (World Rowing)

item.title: Current Events - September 06, 2026
item.description:
September 6, 2026 (2026-09-06) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
    • Four people are killed and 20 more injured in a series of Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon. (Al Jazeera)

Disasters and accidents

  • Jakarta's Soekarno–Hatta International Airport, Indonesia's busiest airport, suspends flight operations after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatoa reaches the airport. (AFP via ABS-CBN News)

Law and crime

  • A shooting five days ago outside a bar frequented by LGBTQ people in Tucson, Arizona, United States, which left three people killed, including the perpetrator, is confirmed to be motivated in homophobia. (Tucson Sentinel)

item.title: Current Events - August 29, 2026
item.description:
August 29, 2026 (2026-08-29) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • A tanker is struck by a unknown projectile while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz near Khasab, Oman, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations. (Middle East Eye)
    • Gaza war
      • Attacks on health facilities during the Gaza war
        • Israel strikes the Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital in the Deir al-Balah area of the Gaza Strip, killing three people, in violation of the October 2025 ceasefire. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) stated that they targeted a Hamas commander who, according to it, was hiding within the compound of the hospital. (MENA via The New Arab)
      • The IDF confirms that they have killed Nukhba Force commander Hani Abd al-Hai Fakhri Mazloum and Hamas sniper Hassan Zidan Hassan Deiri in separate strikes in the northern Gaza Strip. (The Times of Israel)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Ukrainian drone attack on Shebekino, Belgorod Oblast, Russia, kills three people and damages residential buildings, according to the regional emergency response center. (Xinhua)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Piracy off the coast of Somalia
      • The Cameroon-flagged Turkish cargo ship MV LUTUF, which was hijacked on August 17, is freed by Somali and Turkish forces off the coast of Somalia. Conversely, the Puntland ministry of security says a ransom was paid. (AP) (Garowe Online) (Hiiraan Online)
  • 2026 Nigerien coup attempt
    • Nigerien television confirms that dissenting elements of the Niger Armed Forces attempted a coup in the nation's capital, Niamey. Attacks are reported on Diori Hamani International Airport and the Presidential Palace. (AP) (Reuters)
  • Mali War
    • Tuareg rebels free 60 Malian soldiers in exchange for army officer-turned-defector Inkinane Ag Attaher. (Al Jazeera)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Nepal floods
    • The death toll from flash floods in Nepal rises to 669, with more than 2,400 people reported missing. (NBC News)
  • A flash flood in the Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona, United States, leaves about 15 people missing and prompts the evacuation of at least 62 others. (AFP via France 24)
  • A person is rescued while four people are missing when a sport utility vehicle plunges into a river after a bridge in Tarlac City, Philippines, collapses. The bridge has been serving as an alternative route as another partially collapsed days prior amid monsoon rains. (Philippine Daily Inquirer)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Icelandic European Union membership negotiations referendum
    • Iceland rejects restarting membership negotiations with the EU in a referendum. (RÚV)

Sports

  • 2026 Women's FIH Hockey World Cup
    • 2026 Women's FIH Hockey World Cup final
      • In field hockey, Argentina beat the Netherlands in the final after a 1–1 draw and a penalty shoot-out to secure their third Women's World Cup title. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Women's NORCECA Volleyball Championship
    • Canada at the 2028 Summer Olympics, Volleyball at the 2028 Summer Olympics
      • In volleyball, the Canadian women’s national team qualifies for the upcoming Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, California, U.S., their first qualification since 1996 following a victory against the Dominican Republic in the Women's NORCECA Volleyball Continental Championship. (CBC)
  • Moses Itauma vs Filip Hrgovic
    • In boxing, Filip Hrgović defeats Moses Itauma by ninth-round stoppage to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title. Hrgović becomes the first Croatian heavyweight boxing world champion. (AFP via The Philippine Star)
  • In tennis, former player Roger Federer is inducted into the player category, while former player and current sportscaster Mary Carillo is inducted into the contributor category of the International Tennis Hall of Fame respectively. (Sports Business Journal)

item.title: Current Events - September 05, 2026
item.description:
September 5, 2026 (2026-09-05) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russia and Ukraine agree to halt strikes on Kyiv and Moscow, respectively, during United States-mediated peace talks, as U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff meet Russian president Vladimir Putin in Moscow before traveling to Kyiv. (AFP via Dawn)
    • Kyiv strikes
      • A Russian missile strike kills two people and damages multiple residential buildings in Bucha, Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine. (UA News)
    • Russian occupation of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast
      • A Russian airstrike on Kamianske, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine, kills four people and injures five others, including one critically, according to Dnipropetrovsk governor Oleksandr Hanza. (SANA)
  • 2026 Iran war
    • The United States Central Command says its forces have destroyed three Iranian oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including one in the Gulf of Oman, after alleged Iranian missile attacks on U.S. naval vessels. (AFP via France 24) (BBC News)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Pacific typhoon season
    • Typhoon Saudel
      • One person is killed and eleven others are reported missing after a mudslide buries a village and damages 12 homes in Suichuan County, Jiangxi, China. (AP)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • Indonesia's disaster agency and air force conduct aerial firefighting operations to contain wildfires near the planned capital Nusantara in East Kalimantan, following a request from the Nusantara Capital City Authority. (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)
  • At least 21 people are killed and several others are injured after a bus carrying mostly secondary school students plunges down a slope in Fogo island, Cape Verde. (Xinhua)
  • Ten people are killed and six others are injured after a tanker truck suffers a break failure and explodes on the Hamedan–Sanandaj highway, Iran (Street Insider)
  • A Greek F-4 Phantom jet crashes during an air show at Tanagra Air Base near Athens, Greece, killing both pilots. (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • Tens of thousands of people rally in Zagreb, Croatia, demanding the removal of about 37,000 tonnes of illegally dumped hazardous waste from Gospić and a ban on waste imports amid concerns over soil and groundwater contamination. (AP)
  • The National Food Agency of Indonesia reports that nearly 2,000 people, mostly students, have fallen ill across the country this week in suspected food poisoning outbreaks linked to president Prabowo Subianto's new Free Nutritious Meals program. (AP)

International relations

  • The 128 parties to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons agree on a non-binding text defining lethal autonomous weapons systems, potentially enabling negotiations on international rules governing their use. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Peruvian security crisis
    • Peru declares a 60-day state of emergency in five supermax prisons, authorizing police and military forces to control the facilities and surrounding airspace and communications to disrupt criminal organizations operating from prisons. (Reuters)
  • United Kingdom anti-immigration protests
    • Hundreds of masked anti-immigration protesters block the Port of Dover in Kent, England, and chant "stop the boats", causing massive disruption to traffic and train services. (BBC News) (CNN)
  • Philippine vice president Sara Duterte posts ₱360,000 (US$5,740) bail on three counts of grave threats, prompting a regional trial court to lift her arrest warrant. The charges concern alleged threats against president Bongbong Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. (AP)
  • In Egypt, twelve people are sentenced to death for drugs trafficking, including television presenter Sarah Khalifa. (AFP via ABC News Australia)

Sports

  • 2026 Formula One World Championship
    • 2026 Italian Grand Prix
      • In Formula One, Aston Martin driver Lance Stroll becomes the first driver to be knocked out in Q1 100 times after doing so at the 2026 Italian Grand Prix. (Motorsport)
      • At the same Grand Prix, Alpine driver Pierre Gasly achieves his maiden pole position after qualifying first, the first French driver to do so since Jean Alesi in 1997. (F1) (USA Today)
  • 2026 China GT Championship
    • Dutch Loek Hartog rescues fellow driver Ollie Millroy [de] from a burning car following an accident at the Shanghai International Circuit. (Motorsport Network)
  • 2026 Diamond League
    • 2026 Memorial Van Damme
      • In track and field, Swiss athlete Audrey Werro wins the women's 800 metres at the Diamond League's Memorial Van Damme in Brussels, Belgium, with a meeting record of 1:54.75. (Athletics Weekly)
  • 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup
    • In women's basketball, the Mali women's national basketball team upsets Spain 82-73, making it Mali's second ever victory in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup after its 2010 victory against Senegal. (The Guardian) (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - August 31, 2026
item.description:
August 31, 2026 (2026-08-31) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says that a supertanker caught fire after hitting two naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC accuses the United States of responsibility for the attack, which the United States Central Command on an X post denies. (The Guardian) (Reuters via Arab News)
      • United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war
        • The United Arab Emirates defense ministry reports that an Iranian drone has been intercepted over the country's airspace. Additionally, Iran's army says that they have attacked the Al Minhad Air Base, which the UAE denies. (AP)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip kill ⁠at least five people. (Al Jazeera)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Aerial warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Kyiv strikes
      • Ukraine tightens security measures for Kyiv's public transport, schools, and parliament amid increased Russian drone attacks, including restrictions on large school gatherings, possible remote learning, and expanded shelter arrangements. (AFP via Bangkok Post)
  • Colombian conflict
    • A car bomb outside a police station in Los Patios, Norte de Santander, Colombia, kills one civilian and injures 11 others, including two officers. Police attribute the attack to the National Liberation Army. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Nepal floods
    • It is reported that school principal Rajendra Dawadi saved over 900 students and 16 faculty members at the Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur, Nuwakot District, Nepal, 10 minutes before flash floods hit the area last week. (AP) (Reuters)
    • The death toll from the flash floods in Nepal has reached past 950. Additionally, hundreds are reported to be feared stuck in hydropower tunnels in wake of the floods. (AP) (CBC)
  • 2026 Grand Canyon flood
    • The death toll from the flash flood in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona, United States, last Saturday rises to two, while the number of people missing falls from more than 20 to one after park rangers locate most of those previously unaccounted for. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • The Mount Sinabung stratovolcano in North Sumatra, Indonesia, erupts, sending 3,500 meters of ash in the air. Residents and visitors around Lake Lau Kawar are ordered to evacuate. (AA) (Antara News)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The total amount of cases of ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 6,000. (Al Jazeera)
  • A data from the Methane Alert and Response System reports that Turkmenistan has started the process of clearing methane leaks from its oil and gas facilities. (The Guardian)

International relations

  • 2026 Bishkek SCO summit
    • The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit is held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, which coincides with the country's Independence Day and the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Nomad Games. (The Times of Central Asia) (Xinhua)
  • Greece–Israel relations, 2020s European rearmament
    • Israel and Greece sign a €3 billion (US$3.48 billion) arms export deal that will enable the Israeli defense ministry to build the "Achilles Shield", a multi-layered air defense array similar to the Iron Dome, made entirely by Israeli systems, including David's Sling, SPYDER, and Barak MX. (DW) (The Jerusalem Post)
  • India–Pakistan wars and conflicts
    • The Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague, Netherlands, orders India to comply with the Indus Waters Treaty and restrict work on two hydroelectric projects that could violate it. India rejects the ruling and maintains that the treaty remains suspended. (AFP via France 24)
  • Italy–Spain relations, 2026 Ceuta migrant crisis
    • Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni announces that Italy will extend its suspension of the Schengen free movement agreement with Spain for another 15 days in response to the migrant crisis event at the Ceuta border fence with Morocco. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Corruption in South Korea, Unification Church and politics
    • A South Korean court sentences Unification Church leader Hak Ja Han to two years in prison for bribing officials, including former first lady Kim Keon Hee, in an effort to obtain policy favors. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
  • Kidnapping of Shelly Kittleson
    • A judiciary in Iraq sentences Kata'ib Hezbollah member Amir Rahim Jabbar to 15 years in prison for his role in the kidnapping of American journalist Shelly Kittleson. (Asharq Al Awsat)
  • Murder of Tupac Shakur
    • A jury in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States, finds former Crips gang leader Duane Davis guilty of first-degree murder for orchestrating the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur during a drive-by shooting in Paradise in 1996. (ABC News) (BBC News)
  • A tribunal of first instance in Brussels, Belgium, orders biometrics company Semlex and 13 other defendants to stand trial over alleged corruption, money laundering, and tax fraud linked to a passport contract in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. (Reuters)
  • A suspect is arrested in relation to a mass shooting over the weekend at a rave in Aarau, Aargau, Switzerland, which killed a woman and injured five other people. (DW)
  • A woman stabs two people in Times Square, New York City, U.S., killing a Bank of America vice president and injuring another person, before police fatally shot her after she refused commands to drop her knives. (AFP via France 24) (Al Jazeera)

Politics and elections

  • 2025–2026 Kosovo political deadlock
    • Kosovo's Vetëvendosje and Democratic League parties agree to support former Constitutional Court judge Bekim Sejdiu for president, potentially ending nearly two years of political deadlock and enabling the formation of a new government. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • AI boom
    • Adobe Inc. reaches a US$4 billion deal to offer free access to AI tools in Saudi Arabia with its Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and Humain. (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - August 24, 2026
item.description:
August 24, 2026 (2026-08-24) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Operation Southern Spear
    • United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
      • The U.S. military Southern Command's Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere launches a strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean on alleged drug traffickers, killing two people. The strike is the first reported in two months. (PBS) (CNN)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukraine–United Kingdom relations
      • During a visit to Kyiv, Ukraine, British prime minister Andy Burnham confirms that he has approved supplying Ukraine with the classified blueprints to produce Storm Shadow cruise missiles despite Russian threats against such a move, which will give Ukrainian forces the ability to strike key targets deep inside Russian territory. (BBC News)
    • Kharkiv strikes
      • A Russian missile strike on the outskirts of Kharkiv kills three people and leaves eight others wounded. (TRT World)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Darfur campaign
      • Drone strikes by the Sudanese Armed Forces hits several Rapid Support Forces Paramilitary targets in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan, hours after a cargo aircraft landed in the area. (Sudan Tribune)
  • South Sudanese Civil War
    • Jonglei clashes
      • Two peacekeepers from Ethiopia of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan are killed in an ambush by unknown gunmen in Jonglei State, South Sudan. Three more peacekeepers, two policemen and two civilians are also wounded. (RFI in French)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • International sanctions against Iran, United States sanctions against Iran
      • U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announces Operation Economic Outcast, a campaign involving new sanctions against Iran in a effort to isolate the regime. (The Wall Street Journal) (Politico)
    • Iranian economic crisis
      • The Iranian rial reaches 2.02 million rials ahead of the U.S. dollar, a record-low, ahead of U.S. sanctions. (Time)

Health and environment

  • 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
    • The Arkansas Department of Health reports seven new cases of cyclosporiasis in the state, including the first cases in Ashley and Cleburne counties, amidst a decline in the outbreak across the United States. (Arkansas Democrat-Gazette)

International relations

  • Armenia–European Union relations, Enlargement of the European Union
    • Accession of Armenia to the European Union
      • Armenian prime minister Nikol Pashinyan announces that the country will soon formally apply for membership of the European Union. (TASS)
  • Syria–United States relations
    • The United States formally removes Syria from its designated state sponsors of terrorism list. (The Straits Times) (The Jerusalem Post)

Law and crime

  • Syria's Grand Mufti Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun is found guilty of committing war crimes spanning nearly 14 years of civil war under Bashar al-Assad's former regime and is sentenced to life in prison. (AP) (Al Jazeera) (DW)
  • Former British snooker player Graeme Dott is found guilty of sexually abusing two primary school children. (The Guardian) (Sky News)
  • South African police arrests four people in connection of the murder of former professional boxer Zolani Tete. (Sahara Reporters) (Al Jazeera)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Kazakh legislative election
    • The Central Election Commission of Kazakhstan declares the preliminary results from yesterday's election, stating that Ädilet secured 71% of the vote. (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - August 28, 2026
item.description:
August 28, 2026 (2026-08-28) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Blue Nile campaign
      • Sudan's Rapid Support Forces (RSF) says that they have seized the Bakori and Surkum army bases in the southeastern Blue Nile region alongside Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North (SPLM–N). (Sudan Tribune)
    • Kordofan campaign
      • Emergency Lawyers, an independent group documenting atrocities in Sudan, reports that eight civilians have been killed in drone strikes in the Sowdari District of North Kordofan. (AP) (Asharq Al Awsat)
  • Gaza war
    • Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
      • The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) says that they have killed three Palestinian militants, including Islamic Jihad (PIJ) senior member Qais Bitawi, in a drone strike in the Israel-occupied West Bank city of Jenin. The PIJ also confirms Bitawi's death. (Reuters) (The Times of Israel)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • A Russian drone strike hits a supply depot in Bucha, Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine, triggering explosions and a fire that killed at least 37 people. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says explosives stored near homes worsened the disaster. (CNN)

Business and economy

  • The Japanese finance ministry says it spent a record ¥15.4 trillion (US$96 billion) between July 30 and August 26 to support the yen, marking the country's largest monthly currency intervention on record. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • Twenty-seven people are killed and seven people are injured after a vehicle carrying churchgoers collided head-on with a truck in Chivhu, Zimbabwe. (MSN)

Health and environment

  • Seventh cholera pandemic
    • Nigeria records 65,000 cases of cholera, across 35 states, alongside 10,000 cases of diphtheria. Additionally, NCDC director Jide Idris reports a decline in cholera cases but also warn that transmission of cases remain ongoing. (The Nation NG) (Daily Trust)

International relations

  • United States–Venezuela relations
    • The United States and Venezuela agree to expand U.S. access to Venezuelan oil reserves under a deal involving US$100 billion in private investment, while Venezuela retains ownership of its petroleum resources. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Corruption in Ecuador
    • An Ecuadorian court convicts former president Lenín Moreno of bribery linked to the construction of the Coca Codo Sinclair plant in Napo Province. His wife, Rocío González Navas, and daughter are also found guilty. (Reuters)
  • Protests against Donald Trump
    • Demonstrators gather in Washington, D.C., United States, to protest against the Trump administration's alleged efforts to rollback voting and civil rights, 63 years after the March on Washington rally by civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. (Reuters)
  • Scam centers in Cambodia
    • The Cambodian government says that they have closed more than 700 online scam centers and arrested nearly 30,000 suspects, including 15 senior officials and law-enforcement officers, during a year-long crackdown on cybercrime networks. (Euronews)
  • Two men steal a 200-carat platinum-and-diamond necklace from the Museum of Applied Arts in Vienna, Austria, after smashing a display case with a hammer and fleeing, according to Austrian police. (AFP via CBS News)
  • Two teenagers are arrested in Israel for allegedly pledging allegiance to ISIS and plotting an attack on security forces at the Temple Mount and an IDF base in northern Israel. (Ynetnews) (The Times of Israel)

Politics and elections

  • Death and state funeral of Harald V
    • King Harald V of Norway dies at the age of 89 after a 35-year reign and is succeeded by his son Haakon VIII. (AP) (BBC News) (CNN)
  • Forced contraception of women in Greenland
    • Greenland establishes a truth and reconciliation commission after experts conclude that a decades-long Danish contraceptive program violated Inuit women's rights but disagree on whether it constituted genocide. (Al Jazeera)
  • Serbia justice minister Nenad Vujić says that convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić will be buried with state and military honors following his death at the United Nations Detention Unit at the Hague. (CNN) (Serbian Times)

Sports

  • 2026–27 NHL season
    • In ice hockey, the Colorado Avalanche sign defenceman and alternate captain Cale Makar to an eight-year extension worth US$163.2 million, the largest contract in National Hockey League history. He is the first player to exceed $20 million in average annual value. (The Athletic via The New York Times) (CBS Sports) (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - September 04, 2026
item.description:
September 4, 2026 (2026-09-04) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Gaza war
      • Aftermath of the Battle of Sufa
        • The Israel Defense Forces state that Mohammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi, a Nukhba Force commander who participated in the October 7 attacks on the Sufa post, was killed in an airstrike in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip. (The Times of Israel)
    • 2026 Lebanon war
      • 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire
        • Israel frees four prisoners, including two Syrian citizens, via International Committee of the Red Cross as part of efforts to revive U.S.-backed peace talks signed between Israel and Lebanon. (Al Jazeera) (The Hill)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Over 120 people are confirmed to have been killed since yesterday during the clashes between Houthis and the Yemeni Armed Forces in western Yemen. (AFP via France 24)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Kyiv strikes
      • A Russian drone strikes the Security Service of Ukraine (SSU) headquarters in central Kyiv, injuring five people. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says the attack targeted acting SSU head Oleksandr Poklad, who was unharmed. (CNN)
  • Colombian conflict
    • At least three soldiers are killed and four are wounded by explosives dropped from drones in Ocaña, Norte de Santander, Colombia. Local authorities blame the attack on the National Liberation Army. (AP)
  • Insurgency in Balochistan
    • The Pakistani military says it has killed 48 Baloch seperatists in a series of raids on hideouts over the past 72 hours in Balochistan, Pakistan. (AP)
  • Kidnapping in Nigeria
    • Nine people, including five Department of State Services personnel, are killed during a security operation to rescue kidnapped victims in Oyo State, Nigeria. (Vanguard)

Arts and culture

  • An Argentine judge orders the repatriation of Giacomo Ceruti's 18th-century painting Portrait of a Lady, looted by Nazi Germany from Dutch Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker during World War II, to Goudstikker's daughter-in-law Marei von Saher. (AFP via France 24)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
      • The American Automobile Association reports that the average U.S. diesel price reached a record $5.85 per gallon, up from $3.71 a year earlier, amid disruptions to global energy markets caused by the Iran war. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 European drought, 2026 European heatwaves
    • France allocates more than €1 billion to support farms affected by drought and heatwaves, including compensation for crop losses, liquidity assistance, tax relief, and support for fertilizer and agricultural diesel costs. (The Peninsula)
  • Tajikistan's capital Dushanbe begins construction on the 340-meter-high Dushanbe Tower, which is set to become the tallest building in Central Asia. President Emomali Rahmon and Mayor Rustami Emomali laying the building's foundation stone. (Asia-News) (Caspian Post) (The Gulf Observer)
  • The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opens an investigation into whether Tesla's new Cybercab robotaxi models are properly certified and demonstrates compliance with motor vehicle safety standards. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Nepal floods
    • The Nepali Army rescues two people from a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station in Rasuwa District, a week after floods ravaged the country. (NBC News)
  • Around 22 people are killed in a blaze of unknown origin at a wedding party in Lingwala, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. (AP)
  • At least two people are killed, 62 others sustain injuries, and 14 others remain unaccounted for after a blast at a military base storing pyrotechnic material in Viacha, Bolivia. (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • 2026 East Malaysia haze
    • Malaysia declares a state of emergency in Serian Division, Sarawak, after haze from wildfires in nearby Kalimantan, Indonesia, pushed air pollution above hazardous levels, closing 647 schools. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Democratic Republic of the Congo issues an updated 180-day response to the Ebola outbreak in the country. (Xinhua)
  • New Zealand becomes the second country after Australia to authorize pharmaceutical-grade MDMA for severe post-traumatic stress disorder, with Medsafe allowing two psychiatrists to prescribe it alongside psychotherapy in controlled clinical settings. (AFP via France 24)

International relations

  • Cambodia–United States relations
    • The Royal Cambodian Army announces that they will resume joint military exercises with the United States beginning in February 2027 after they were suspended in 2017. The exercise will be codenamed Exercise Angkor Sentinel. (AP)
  • The United Nations General Assembly adopts a resolution supporting the Equal Earth map projection over the Mercator projection, with 164 countries voting in favor, one against (United States), and six abstaining. (The Guardian)
  • European Union enlargement chief Marta Kos cancels a visit to Serbia after a Serbian government plane took the remains of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić to Belgrade for his funeral. (AP) (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Killing of the Clancy children
    • In the United States, Massachusetts Superior Court associate justice William F. Sullivan declares a mistrial in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial after jurors were deadlocked following more than 38 hours of deliberations, with the panel split 11–1. (BBC News) (The Guardian)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Mexico's navy, the attorney general, and the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection seize approximately 16.8 tonnes of methamphetamine and dismantle three clandestine drug laboratories in Sinaloa. (AFP via Arab News)
  • Mexican federal deputy Zenyazen Escobar García is found dead inside his vehicle in his home state of Veracruz with at least one gunshot wound. State prosecutors open an investigation without determining whether his death is suicide or homicide. (AFP via The Manila Times)
  • A Philippine regional trial court issues an arrest warrant for vice president Sara Duterte on three counts of grave threats against president Bongbong Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez, setting bail at ₱120,000 (US$2,000) per count. (Reuters)
  • Police in Guangxi, China, arrest 52 Singaporeans over suspected involvement in illegal pyramid-scheme activities as part of a broader law-enforcement operation. Singapore's foreign ministry says it is providing consular assistance. (Reuters)
  • Sri Lankan MP Namal Rajapaksa is arrested over alleged corruption involving SriLankan Airlines' 2013 Airbus purchases. A court in Colombo remands him until September 18. (Reuters)
  • A Tunisian judge orders journalist Mohamed Ali Yousfi detained on allegations of illicit enrichment, money laundering, and conspiracy after police arrest him outside Express FM in Tunis. (DW)

Politics and elections

  • Meloni government
    • Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government becomes the longest serving in Italy during the postwar era. (DW)
  • The remains of King Rukidi IV of the Tooro Kingdom return to Uganda for his burial. (BBC News) (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup
    • The opening ceremony for the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup is held in Berlin, Germany, with the defending champions United States defeating China 94–61. (AP)
